I've been working this land since I was 20. I know every corner of it. My two sons work in the county town now, so it's mostly me and my wife. I need to be practical — I can't take on too much labor-intensive work anymore at 60.

**My thinking:**

I'll keep 10 mu in the wheat-maize rotation I've done for decades. That's reliable. For wheat I'll use the Jimai improved variety — I know it, the seed station has it, it yields steadily here. Four irrigations for wheat is what this land needs: at sowing, wintering, jointing, and grain filling. Skip any of those and the yield drops badly, I've seen it. I'll apply compound fertilizer as base dressing and add urea at the jointing stage, same as always.

For summer maize after the wheat harvest, I'll direct-seed with Xianyu hybrid seed right into the stubble — no-till saves me time and my back, and I need to get it in fast while there's soil moisture. Three irrigations usually gets me through unless it rains decent in July.

The remaining 5 mu I'll put in cotton for cash. Cotton is more work but I've grown it my whole life. I'll use Bt hybrid cotton — it saves me a few pesticide sprays compared to the old days. Still need five applications though, the bollworm pressure here is real. I'll plough that field in spring before planting. Cotton needs potassium, so I put a bit more of that in.

I won't change what works. My yields aren't record-breaking but they're consistent, and I know what inputs I need.
